scenes.headline: How a stack of effects becomes few GPU passes
scenes.sub: Inside the engine Shaders just released under MIT
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Texel! Shaders just opened its WebGPU engine. The effects are nice. The compiler under them is the interesting part.

scenes.text: Shaders compiles your whole layer tree into as few GPU passes as it can, and only rebuilds when the tree's shape changes.
scenes.say: The engine compiles your whole layer tree into as few GPU passes as it can, and rebuilds only when its shape changes.

scenes.label: effect components, each a plain object of props and one paint function
scenes.say: Each of the one hundred and ninety nine effects is a plain object: props, and one function saying what to draw.

steps.say: The composer walks your tree and builds one expression for every pixel.
Gradients, noise and colour filters stay inline. They blend in registers, in a single fragment function.
A filter that reads neighbouring pixels, like a blur, cannot work on an expression. Everything below it is rendered to a texture first.

scenes.title: Why a twirl needs no texture

parts.note: the twirl only moves the coordinate
parts.say: A twirl does not change colours. It only moves the coordinate it reads from.

parts.note: evaluate each layer at the moved point
parts.say: So the engine evaluates each layer at the moved point. No texture, and no softening from resampling.

items.say: Change a colour or a speed, and it is one write into a single packed uniform buffer.
Change a prop that alters the code, like edge handling, and a structural hash changes.
The new pipeline builds while the old one keeps drawing, so nothing flashes.

steps.say: This is the design editor. Every layer here is a component in that tree.
And every control in this panel is a uniform write, unless the prop is compile time.

scenes.text: Stack colour effects freely; every blur-like filter costs a full-frame texture, so nest distortions around layers.
scenes.say: Stack colour effects freely. Each blur-like filter costs a full-frame texture. And wrap distortions around their layers.
Layers fuse. Gather filters add a texture. Props are just uniform writes.
